word_order: SVO | Most full clauses in the sample place a nominal subject before a verb and then objects/adjuncts (e.g. "He did give", "The capsule will look", "Israel demands an ongoing ...").
register: formal written expository prose (news, encyclopedia, technical summaries) rather than spontaneous speech
non_boundary_traps: noun-internal appositives and modifiers (e.g. titles like "Sir", company names)
notes_for_prompt_writer: Sentences are formal, mostly multi-clausal, and rely heavily on subordinating conjunctions and relative pronouns to introduce embedded clauses. Commas frequently set off appositives, participial phrases and adjuncts rather than marking clause completion. Possessive 's and prepositional phrases are typically internal to noun phrases and should not be treated as clause boundaries. There are essentially no spoken hesitations in this register.
